Model keys sign_standing / sign_wall / hanging_sign_wall / hanging_sign_ceiling / hanging_sign_ceiling_middle (:2822-2831), registered in the MODELS table at :1426-1434 to the oak entity-model layers, with per-wood texture signs::board_texture (signs.rs:333, entity/signs/{wood}). items.evidence: No horizon-prepare run has produced client resources in this worktree: versions/1.21.11/.local holds only Batch 0's measure-oracles/ and the mappings/research dir minecraft/1.21.11/ (jars, libraries, manifest, prepared.json, remapped.json, reports, sources) — no horizon-client/ resources at all, and a find over the whole .local returns no sounds.json anywhere. The flow defect is verified in-tree: horizon-prepare has a separate sounds subcommand (crates/horizon-prepare/src/main.rs:24) and --complete copies sounds (:55, :275-282), but --prepare alone does not (:230). The client then fails silently: SoundRegistry::load (horizon-client-render/src/sound_events.rs:262) reads each namespace's sounds.json with let Ok(text) = fs::read(...) else { continue; } (:280-282) — a missing file is skipped without a word. With an empty registry the game plays no event sound at all. The 6 audio_harness drivers (ambient_sound, audio_attributes, music, situational_music, sound_engine, sound_event) all call require_sounds() (tools/audio_harness.py:35) and are data-gated by this item — and unlike 1.21.10, sound_event is oracle-clean now, so the sounds step alone would make it runnable; the other five are oracle-blocked too (B10-O04). The wiring itself is fine (report §4 check 1: 1,837 sounds.json events vs 1,838 registry events, only intentionally_empty missing, zero orphans): the failure is the missing file, not a mismatch.
items.title: No sounds.json in the prepared 1.21.11 resources: the game is silent and 6 audio drivers cannot run

items.evidence: Both halves reproduce. PLACED: vanilla 1.21.11 renders beds through BedRenderer (createHeadLayer / createFootLayer / submitPiece, registered for BlockEntityType.BED — javap-ber.txt, ber-types.txt); the block model is particle-only (models/block/bed.json, all bed blockstates point at it), so there is no terrain-mesh fallback. The port has no bed draw path: the Kind enum (block_entity_render.rs:323) has no Bed variant, no Kind::Bed arm exists anywhere, the only bed mention in the file is the lowercase 'beds' in the stale :1020 comment, item_render/special.rs has 0 bed mentions, game/beds.rs is sleep mechanics only. ITEMS: vanilla 1.21.11's items/red_bed.json (all 16 colours) is a SINGLE minecraft:special with type minecraft:bed + texture — the 1.21.7 form, not 26.1.2's composite-of-two (1.21.11 has no composite model type). The port's SpecialModel::decode (horizon-assets/src/item_model/special.rs:82) has NO bed arm (ten arms: banner, conduit, chest, copper_golem_statue, decorated_pot, head, player_head, shulker_box, shield, trident — :89-135); the header doc (:1-8) states it: 'Bed, standing-sign and hanging-sign types exist in 1.21.11's registry but have no kind here yet: a model naming one fails to decode and the item falls back to the missing model'. The error propagates via ? (item_model.rs:489-491); load_definitions (horizon-client/src/item_render.rs:691) skips the item; append_layers renders the missing model (item_model.rs:1110, state.missing(out)). All 16 bed items render as the missing model — proven statically. Standing/hanging-sign specials are also undecodable but no bundled 1.21.11 item definition uses them (census §4 check 13).
items.title: Beds are invisible when placed, AND bed items fail to decode (missing model)

items.evidence: NEVER EXISTED for 1.21.11. The 1.21.7/1.21.10 item's premise inverts here: vanilla 1.21.11 HAS the swap ticker. LivingEntity carries the protected field itemSwapTicker (javap-livingentity-server.txt:129), and Player has getItemSwapScale(float) (javap-player-client.txt:244) — neither exists in 1.21.10. Both sides emit the columns and agree: the probe (crates/horizon-client/examples/probe/first_person_probe.rs, 472 lines) emits strength.swap_ticker and swap_scale at :379-380, and the oracle (VanillaFirstPersonOracle.java:421) emits swapTicker.getInt(player) + player.getItemSwapScale(1.0F) (field looked up at :268, incremented at :398). The oracle PASSES against the 1.21.11 jar (the template's oracle was rewritten for the classic swing model and keeps the swap columns, which are valid here). There is no format mismatch to fix on either side. (Swap-scale VALUES still need the driver run — and the driver is runnable now.) The three-way split is consistent because the vanilla spec differs per version: gap for 1.21.7, fixed for 1.21.10, never existed for 1.21.11.
items.title: First-person probe emits swap-ticker columns the repaired oracle drops — NEVER EXISTED for 1.21.11 (vanilla has the ticker; probe + oracle agree)

items.evidence: NEVER EXISTED for 1.21.11. The 26.1.2 gap's premise does not exist here: vanilla 1.21.11 has NO baby guard. AnimationUtils.animateZombieArms is the 4-arg generic form (ModelPart, ModelPart, boolean, T extends UndeadRenderState) — it reads swingAnimationType (STAB check) and attackTime from the render state, with NO baby/item check (0 isBaby / getMainHandItem occurrences, javap-animationutils-c.txt), and AbstractZombieModel.setupAnim calls it unconditionally, gated only on isAggressive (javap-zombiemodel.txt). The baby guard is a 26.1 addition — it postdates 1.21.11. The port matches vanilla 1.21.11 exactly: mobs/anim.rs:634-636 ('1.21.11 has no baby guard, so a baby holding an item raises its arms like an adult (26.1 returned early for a baby with a main-hand item)') plus the unit test a_baby_zombie_holding_an_item_raises_its_arms_like_an_adult (:1668). A baby zombie holding an item raising its arms IS vanilla 1.21.11 behaviour.
items.title: Baby zombie holding an item lowers its arms instead of keeping them down — NEVER EXISTED for 1.21.11 (vanilla has no baby guard; the port matches)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11's swing is plain fields: swinging / swingTime / swingingArm / attackAnim / oAttackAnim (javap-livingentity-server.txt:105-129); there is no SwingState class and no FirstPersonHandsAndItems class anywhere in the jar (both named in the port's own doc comment, first_person.rs:1-2). getCurrentSwingDuration() is private and reads the held item's swing animation — getItemInHand(MAIN_HAND).getSwingAnimation().duration() — adjusted by haste (duration-(1+amp)) / fatigue (duration+(1+amp)*2) (:4884-4921); swing(hand[, boolean]) restarts only when !swinging || swingTime >= duration/2 || swingTime < 0 (:4930-4959); updateSwingTime() re-reads the duration each tick and resets at duration, so attackAnim never reaches 1.0 (:5456-5490). The port carries the 26.3 form: SwingDescription / SwingState (horizon-client/src/first_person.rs:490-499); start_if_able allows a restart at ticks==0 where vanilla blocks it (:507-522); tick() holds the animation at 1.0 an extra tick (clears only when ticks > duration, :528-541); the duration is cached at swing start where vanilla re-reads effects each tick. (swing_duration, :564, matches vanilla's formula for the per-item animation — the formula is right, the state machine around it is not. Unlike 1.21.10, vanilla 1.21.11 HAS per-item swing animation — the swing_animation component is in the 104-component registry — so the formula match is real here.)
items.title: First-person swing uses the 26.3 SwingState state machine vanilla 1.21.11 does not have

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 resolves sherd patterns via DecoratedPotPatterns.getPatternFromItem(Item) (javap-potpatterns.txt — a static item-to-pattern map; no provides_pottery_pattern anywhere in the class). The port reads the 26.3 component instead: components["minecraft:provides_pottery_pattern"] (block_entity_render.rs:1540, in the sherd-item scan at :1528-1552). That component is ABSENT from 1.21.11's 104-component registry, and there is no data/minecraft/decorated_pot_pattern/ directory in the datagen output — so pot_patterns stays empty and every sherd side falls back to blank (:2469, :3193). The registry lists 24 patterns, unreachable through the component path. (The port's DATA_COMPONENT_TYPES list itself is exact — 104/104, zero drift either way, verified against the registry — so this is a lookup-path defect, not a list defect; the 26.1.2 latent-drift note does not apply here.)
items.title: Decorated-pot sherd patterns never resolve: every side renders blank

items.evidence: Vanilla items/filled_map.json tints with minecraft:constant (-1) + minecraft:map_color (default 4603950). The port's TintSource (horizon-assets/src/item_model.rs:551-559) has NO Map variant; the decode fallthrough returns Err("unknown item tint source") (:588), propagating via ? so the definition is skipped at load and the item renders as the missing model (same load path as bed items, B10-G03). The census (§4 check 13) shows map_color appears in exactly one bundled item definition (filled_map.json), so the blast radius is one item — but it is the map every player holds. (minecraft:map_color IS in the port's DATA_COMPONENT_TYPES list, item_model.rs:86 — the component is known; only the tint source is missing.)
items.title: filled_map fails item decode: the map_color tint source is gone

items.evidence: Vanilla LocalPlayer.swing calls AbstractClientPlayer.swing(hand) then UNCONDITIONALLY sends ServerboundSwingPacket(hand) (javap-localplayer.txt:672-682); the server's handleAnimate resets the last-action time + calls player.swing(hand) (javap-sgpli.txt:4764-4791). The port's swing_hand (game/hand.rs:210-232) sends NOTHING — it only records an Animate packet if the session is recording. The only three S::Swing sends left in the tree are attack paths (game/remote.rs:9936, :10056, :10063). Item-use swings (placing blocks, using items) are invisible to other players; attack swings still show. (Vanilla 1.21.11 has no SwingSource class at all — the 1.21.10 report's three-valued SwingSource note does not carry here.)

items.evidence: Vanilla LevelEventHandler case 3003 plays the sound itself: WAX_ON particles (UniformInt 3-5) + playLocalSound(pos, HONEYCOMB_WAX_ON, BLOCKS, 1.0, 1.0) (javap-leveleventhandler.txt offsets 3369-3399). HoneycombItem.useOn plays NO sound directly — 3 levelEvent(3003) sites, 0 playSound (javap-honeycomb.txt). The port splits the two halves the 26.3 way: block_particle_event (game/level_particles.rs:35-38) plays particles only for 3003, and the sound comes from item code — wax_on_sound (game.rs:8032, callers :8343/:8362) — which only runs for the local player's own waxing. Another player's (or a dispenser's, or a copper golem's) waxing arrives as a bare 3003 event and is silent. (The other wax call sites exist in the 1.21.11 tree and all play the sound directly from their own code — dispenser wax game/dispenser.rs:2206-2235, copper-golem wax game/copper_golems.rs:506, local honeycomb prediction game/remote.rs:8801/:8809 — so the gap is the event path, not the call sites.)
items.title: 3003 wax-on sound missing from the level-event path: other players' waxing is silent

items.evidence: Vanilla's server sends ONE event: AbstractThrownPotion.onHit → levelEvent(instant? 2007 : 2002, pos, color); ThrownExperienceBottle.onHit → levelEvent(2002, pos, 0xFF385DC6). The client 2002/2007 case plays SPLASH_POTION_BREAK itself on NEUTRAL, pitch nextFloat()*0.1+0.9, after the particles (javap-leveleventhandler.txt offsets 1525-1553). LevelEventHandler is an 82-case lookupswitch with NO 1053/1054/2019/2020 cases (case list extracted). The port maps the sound to 1053/1054 (game.rs:4489, pitch :4508) and its own server sends them (game/potions.rs:1935 for the experience bottle, :1967 for thrown potions, alongside the vanilla 2002/2007 at :1933/:1965) — a closed loop that plays against its own server, but a vanilla-server client (which sends only 2002/2007) hears nothing: the client's 2002/2007 arms are particles-only (game.rs:4355-4362, potion_splash_particles).
items.title: 2002/2007 potion-break sound missing from the event path: potion breaks are silent on a 1.21.11-form server

items.evidence: Vanilla MultiPlayerGameMode.startDestroyBlock plays NOTHING (0 'Sound' occurrences in the method); continueDestroyBlock plays ONLY the hit sound on destroyTicks % 4.0 == 0 (javap-mpgm.txt offsets 198-208) as SimpleSoundInstance(hitSound, BLOCKS, (volume+1)/8, pitch*0.5, unseededRandom, pos); addBreakingBlockEffect has 0 occurrences in the class. The port inverts this: remote_mining's start branch calls breaking_block_effects(hit.pos, hit.face, true) (game/remote.rs:8171, comment: 'startDestroyBlock plays the first hit and crack itself; the server's level events 2019 and 2020 do the rest'), and the continue branch plays NO hit sound locally (remote.rs:8180-8265 — its only audio.play is the block BREAK sound at completion, :8254). The port's own server sends 2019 every tick / 2020 every 4th (game/block_breaking.rs:97-101, destroy_progress_event; client handles 2019/2020 at game.rs:4298-4306) — again a closed loop: against a vanilla 1.21.11 server, which sends neither event (they do not exist in vanilla's LevelEventHandler), the port plays one sound at the first hit and then goes silent for the rest of the dig.
items.title: Digging hit sound plays at START, then never again on a 1.21.11-form server

items.evidence: Vanilla passes SoundSource as a parameter: Shearable.shear(level, source, stack) takes BLOCKS from the dispenser (ShearsDispenseItemBehavior, javap-shear.txt:77/:147) and PLAYERS from player shearing (sheep :294, mushroom cow :877, snow golem :1649, bogged :1930 — javap-shear-species.txt); species shear plays via ServerLevel.playSound(null, this, SOUND, source, 1.0, 1.0) (sheep SHEEP_SHEAR, mushroom cow MOOSHROOM_SHEAR, snow golem SNOW_GOLEM_SHEAR, bogged BOGGED_SHEAR, copper golem COPPER_GOLEM_SHEAR — all five javap-verified); 3003 plays wax-on on BLOCKS. The port's Audio::play derives the source from the event name via settings::sound_source (horizon-client-render/src/settings.rs:18-93, a prefix heuristic with a HOSTILE list of 34): dispenser shear entity.sheep.shear → NEUTRAL, entity.bogged.shear → HOSTILE, wax-on item. → PLAYER — all three should be BLOCKS. The dispenser shear sites use audio.play, not audio.play_on (game/dispenser.rs:1941/1975/1989/2003/2018). The plumbing exists — Audio::play_on has many game-code callers in 1.21.11 (game.rs:4445 portal/AMBIENT, :6147 bubble pop/PLAYERS, game/creatures.rs:5153 projectiles/NEUTRAL, ominous_item_spawner.rs:117, player_equip.rs:83, raids.rs:713, remote.rs:3880/4623/4762, game/commands/world_cmds.rs:635 /playsound) — the shear/wax sites just don't use it.
items.title: Sound categories come from the event NAME, not the call site: shear and wax-on sounds land on the wrong volume slider

items.evidence: NEW. 1.21.11 carries the identical code to the 1.21.7 loading-stick defect (fixed in 1.21.7 by 775a25c2, merged 8123e438): a pause landing after the Login packet and before the load tracker finishes deadlocks three ways — a paused server sends no chunks, the frozen tick never finishes the load tracker, and the loading screen hides the pause menu, so there is no way back. The 1.21.11 tree HAS remote_loading() (game/remote.rs:10906, 'Connected or connecting with no player yet', level-load active with Reason::Other or no player yet) and uses it as a gate elsewhere (mouse input game.rs:10768, native hooks, screen backgrounds, studio) — but NONE of the three pause sites is gated: (1) Escape → pause, play_keys.rs:78-88 (Screen::Playing => screen = Screen::Paused, no gate; 1.21.7 fixed play_keys.rs:91 has 'if self.remote_loading() { return Ok(()); }' with the LevelLoadingScreen.shouldCloseOnEsc comment); (2) pauses_game(), pointer_capture.rs:47-52 (no remote_loading term; 1.21.7 :55 has '&& !self.remote_loading()'); (3) focus-loss pause, pause_if_inactive, pointer_capture.rs:72-95 (no remote_loading term; 1.21.7 :84 has it). Vanilla side confirmed fresh for 1.21.11: LevelLoadingScreen.shouldCloseOnEsc() returns false (javap-levelloading-c.txt: iconst_0; ireturn). The deadlock itself was NOT reproduced headless on the VM (as in 1.21.7, the laptop is where it reproduces directly — probe P12); the code identity is exact. Propagation is a separate owner decision — this batch only CHECKS.
items.method: source comparison vs the 1.21.7 fix + javap
items.title: Pause during terrain load deadlocks the game — the 1.21.7 loading stick, unpropagated (no remote_loading gate on Escape, focus-loss pause, or pauses_game)

systemic_note: Four systemic points. (1) THE TEMPLATE IS WHERE THE SIGN FIX LIVES: 1.21.11 is the E6 era template and the sign-board fix (ac8dd9dc) originated here — B10-G01 is FIXED, and the template's oracle sources were adapted during the port, so six oracles that failed for 1.21.10 PASS here (FirstPerson, ItemModel, PackResources, SoundEvent, ZombieCure, EntityParticles) and 13 of 50 drivers are runnable by javac, the best 1.21.x oracle picture yet. (2) 1.21.11 IS A STEP AHEAD OF 1.21.10 IN VANILLA SCOPE: it has the environment_attribute/game_rule registries, the permissions package, the minecart/zombie/animal subpackages, the SwingAnimation component, the swap ticker, and TextRenderable.Styled — so several 1.21.10 oracle causes vanish, one behaviour item inverts (B10-G05: the swap ticker EXISTS here, so probe and oracle agreeing on the columns is correct), and one item's nuance changes (B10-G08: vanilla HAS per-item swing animation here, so only the state machine is wrong, not the formula). (3) THE SOUND-SIDE CLUSTER REPRODUCES WHOLESALE: the missing sounds.json (B10-G02), three level-event sounds lost to 26.3-form splits (B10-G12/G13/G14 — each a closed loop that plays against the port's own server and goes silent against a vanilla 1.21.11 server), the unsent swing packet (B10-G11), and name-derived sound categories (B10-G15). (4) THE LOADING STICK IS TEMPLATE-LEVEL AND UNPROPAGATED: the 1.21.7 fix (775a25c2) gated all three pause sites on remote_loading(), but the template — which HAS remote_loading() and uses it elsewhere — gates none of them, so the identical deadlock exists in 1.21.11 (B10-G16, new, major). (5) THE ORACLE TABLE CANNOT BE CARRIED ACROSS VERSIONS: 32 of 67 in-scope oracles deviate from the 1.21.10 table, and the oracle SOURCES differ between the trees (the template's repairs), so provisional triage from another version's table is not a fallback for 1.21.11 — this batch measured the table itself with the Batch 0 method, and the real Batch 0 table should be diffed against that measurement when it lands.
